question: What is the main health risk of breathing in silica or asbestos dust over a long time?

options.A: Progressive lung scarring and breathing damage

options.D: Sudden hearing loss in both ears

question: Why do midwives always give iron and folic acid supplements during antenatal care?

question: Once antibodies are released into the bloodstream, what is their primary mission?

question: Why is it difficult to get high health insurance coverage in Nigeria's informal sector?

question: When a hospital is planning space for future needs, what data is most important to look at?

options.B: Patient admission trends and local population changes
options.C: The cost of office furniture and administrative supplies

question: How do daily nursing assessments help hospitals track their overall quality of care?

question: What is the main goal of holding a post-clinical nursing care conference?

question: What is one of the most serious risks when an older adult suffers a fall?

options.A: Severe injury and potential loss of independence

options.D: An automatic increase in their muscle strength

question: What causes the area around an infected wound to swell up?

question: Why is planning ahead for disasters so crucial instead of just reacting when patients arrive?

options.A: Reacting on the spot is illegal under standard Nigerian healthcare labor laws

question: Why do investigators use the 'Five Whys' technique during an incident review?

question: Which major organ in the body is the main target for hepatotropic viruses?

question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy has a very weak immune system. As a nurse, what is your top priority for them?

options.A: Administering live vaccines to boost their active immunity
options.B: Encouraging immediate exposure to crowded public areas
options.C: Stopping all routine vital sign checks to avoid fatigue

question: Why do we use incineration for body tissues and pathological waste?

options.A: To permanently numb the nerves of the entire leg

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is ongoing tracking, while evaluation assesses final results

question: When does NEMA usually send out relief materials like food and shelter items?

options.A: Exclusively to private international manufacturing companies

options.C: Only during annual national budget planning meetings
options.D: Before any potential hazard is even identified or studied

question: Why might a patient's vomit turn a bright green or yellow color?

question: Why do nurses give medications through an IV line instead of having the patient swallow a pill?

options.A: It lasts much longer in the bloodstream than oral pills.

question: Why is treating an infected person usually not enough to stop a parasite outbreak on its own?

options.A: Patients are easily reinfected from their unimproved home environment
options.B: Parasites mutate into viral pathogens inside the human host

question: In patient safety, what is a 'near-miss'?

options.A: An unsafe situation caught before it reaches the patient

options.A: Bone mineral matrix

question: Why do we usually draw blood cultures from two different sites?

question: Why is an open reporting culture so important for fixing hospital errors?

options.A: It allows the hospital to fire careless workers quickly

options.C: It provides the data needed to understand and fix system flaws
options.D: It ensures nurses receive immediate financial bonuses

question: A family member is sitting quietly at the bedside crying after a loss. What is the most caring nursing action?

options.A: Sit quietly beside the family member and offer a comforting presence

question: Why is it dangerous to press down on a waste bag with your hands to create more space?

question: Why do we count water as a nutrient even though it gives us zero calories?

question: What does the 'teach-back' method mean when teaching a patient?

question: What is a frequent complication when anxiety is left unmanaged for years?

explanation: Spot on! National Societies work right inside their own countries, stepping up as local heroes when disasters strike.

question: Why do nurses teach deep breathing exercises to patients who are feeling very anxious?

options.A: It provides a practical, self-managed tool to help lower acute stress
options.B: It forces the patient to fall asleep for hours
options.C: It cures all known infectious diseases in the body
options.D: It permanently replaces the need for any medical doctor

explanation: Deep breathing calms the nervous system down. It's a fantastic, simple tool patients can use anytime to regain control over panic.

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good evaluation?

options.A: Resistance to feedback
options.B: Rater bias and halo effects
options.C: Standardized grading rubrics
options.D: Severe time constraints

explanation: Rubrics actually fix evaluation problems by giving clear guidelines so grading is fair and consistent!

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the plotting of the active phase on a standard partograph typically begin?

options.A: 10 centimeters
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 7 centimeters
options.D: 1 centimeter

explanation: The active phase and routine partograph plotting traditionally commence once the cervix reaches 4 centimeters of dilation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Why is it important to use a mix of different data collection tools during a community diagnosis?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by international pharmaceutical companies
options.B: It reduces the amount of time needed to write the final report
options.C: It helps verify findings and provides a more complete picture of health needs
options.D: It ensures that every single resident is interviewed personally

explanation: Combining surveys, interviews, and observations allows nurses to cross-verify data and understand both numbers and human experiences. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the difference between a 'use-by' date and a 'best-before' date?

options.A: Use-by is for canned goods, while best-before is for fresh meat
options.B: Use-by relates to safety, while best-before relates to quality
options.C: Use-by is set by the government, while best-before is optional
options.D: Use-by means the food is free, while best-before means it is costly

explanation: Spot on! 'Use-by' is about food safety (don't risk food poisoning), while 'best-before' is just about peak flavor and crunch.

question: What is the main job of a structured healthcare network in reproductive health?

options.A: Eliminating the need for patient medical records across facilities
options.B: Replacing all traditional birth attendants with certified surgeons
options.C: Generating revenue for private pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
options.D: Linking different levels of care to ensure seamless service delivery

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare networks connect primary clinics to big hospitals so patients glide smoothly through the system for whatever care they need.

question: What was a major focus of Nigeria's original 1988 National Population Policy?

options.A: Banning traditional birth attendants nationwide
options.B: Mandatory relocation of rural populations to cities
options.C: Providing free university education for all citizens
options.D: Setting a limit on the number of children per woman

explanation: Back in 1988, the policy tried to slow down rapid population growth by suggesting a specific target for how many children a woman should have. It faced a lot of cultural pushback, but that was the main strategy at the time!

question: Why must nurses keep reassessing patients who have already been sorted into a triage category?

options.A: Rescue teams need to change patient names frequently
options.B: Color tags often fall off in wet weather conditions
options.C: Hospital admission clerks require updated paperwork every hour
options.D: A patient's condition can rapidly deteriorate over time

explanation: Exactly! Injuries can hide beneath the surface, meaning a patient who looks stable now could crash and need urgent help a few minutes later.

question: Why is it important to include the family when creating a patient's care plan?

options.A: It legally forces the family to pay all hospital bills
options.B: It ensures the plan fits their routine and improves cooperation
options.C: It stops the doctor from making any changes to the treatment
options.D: It reduces the total number of nursing shifts required

explanation: When families help build the plan, they understand it better and are much more likely to help carry it out at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important for public health teams to supply food and basic items to households in strict quarantine?

options.A: To punish people who refuse to take their prescribed preventive drugs
options.B: To test the cooking skills of local volunteers and community leaders
options.C: To prevent quarantined individuals from leaving their homes to search for food
options.D: To fulfill routine hospital catering regulations for community clinics

explanation: Brilliant! If people have no food at home, they will break quarantine to go to the market, which defeats the whole purpose of keeping them indoors.

question: Why should a nurse pay attention to family dynamics and community decision-makers?

options.A: So the nurse can bypass the patient entirely and speak only to community elders
options.B: To legally transfer medical decision-making rights away from the patient
options.C: To report family members who disagree with modern medical practices to the police
options.D: Because family heads or spouses often influence whether a patient seeks or continues treatment

explanation: Spot on! In many Nigerian communities, family and elders play a massive role in health choices, so winning their support helps the patient heal.

question: You are asked to do a complex procedure you were never taught in school. What should you do?

options.A: Ask a junior student nurse to perform the task instead
options.B: Decline the task and inform the supervisor about lacking training
options.C: Perform the task anyway to avoid upsetting the senior doctor
options.D: Read a quick internet article on the phone and do the procedure

explanation: Never work outside your scope of practice! Speak up and protect your patient (and your license) by admitting what you don't know yet.

question: What is one major limitation of using robots in patient care units?

options.A: Robots require continuous physical lifting from bedside nurses
options.B: Robots lack clinical intuition and cannot interpret subtle human emotional cues
options.C: Robots completely eliminate the need for electronic health records
options.D: Robots are incapable of moving along hospital corridors

explanation: Spot on! Machines follow strict programming. They can never fully replace the warm, empathetic touch and observant eye of a real nurse.

question: What is the main purpose of the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) in the ICU?

options.A: To measure the depth of sedation or level of agitation in a patient
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of intravenous pain medication needed
options.C: To assess the risk of pressure ulcer formation over bony prominences
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs are exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide

explanation: The RASS score helps the whole healthcare team figure out if a patient is resting peacefully, too sleepy, or too restless.

question: What usually happens during data analysis if a research study completely lacks a theoretical framework?

options.A: The institutional review board will reject the final report
options.B: The data collection process becomes completely unnecessary
options.C: The results may be difficult to interpret within a broader scientific context
options.D: The statistical software will automatically generate a new theory

explanation: Spot on. Without a guiding framework, it becomes really hard to explain what your findings actually mean for the nursing profession.

question: A nurse feels stressed because personal values clash with an assigned care duty. What type of conflict is this?

options.A: Intrapersonal conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Intragroup conflict
options.D: Intergroup conflict

explanation: When the battle is inside your own head regarding your values and duties, it's an intrapersonal conflict. You've got this!

question: What is the relationship between the patient's clinical health record and an internal incident report?

options.A: The incident report is an administrative risk document and is kept separate from the clinical chart
options.B: Both documents are legally identical and stored in the exact same physical folder
options.C: The incident report must be copied word-for-word into the progress notes of the chart
options.D: The clinical chart is kept confidential while the incident report is posted publicly

explanation: Incident reports are administrative tools used for quality improvement and remain separate from the clinical medical record. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why is information science an essential pillar for nursing informatics?

options.A: It provides the ethical guidelines for bedside patient care.
options.B: It builds the physical computer towers used at the nurses' station.
options.C: It manufactures the electronic blood pressure cuffs.
options.D: It structures and organizes how clinical data is gathered and analyzed.

explanation: Information science specifically governs how data is organized, structured, and processed to make it meaningful for healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the main risk of having metal pins go through the scalp into the skull bone?

options.A: Permanent hair loss across the forehead
options.B: Local infection and bone inflammation
options.C: Sudden increase in blood pressure
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Anytime the skin is broken by metal pins, bacteria can sneak in, making infection our top worry to watch out for.

question: Why is it best to combine mass media with face-to-face counselling in health campaigns?

options.A: Mass media is always more accurate than anything a nurse can say in person
options.B: Government regulations require both methods to be used simultaneously
options.C: Face-to-face counselling is too expensive to use unless mass media has failed
options.D: Mass media reaches many people quickly, while face-to-face counselling allows personal questions

explanation: Radio and posters help spread the word far and wide fast, but sitting down to talk allows patients to ask questions and clear up personal doubts! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the main body purpose of warning signs like pain and fever?

options.A: To act as warning signals indicating internal distress or disease
options.B: To punish the patient for eating unhealthy foods
options.C: To slow down normal blood circulation in the limbs
options.D: To increase the body weight of an infected person

explanation: Exactly! Think of pain and fever as the body's alarm system alerting you that something inside needs attention.

question: Which of the following is a major infrastructure barrier to EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Frequent power outages and unstable internet connectivity
options.B: Laws that strictly forbid the use of computers in medicine
options.C: Excessive availability of free software for every clinic
options.D: A complete lack of sick patients needing documentation

explanation: Unreliable power supply and poor internet access pose significant daily challenges to maintaining continuous digital health records in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: A patient is due for their blood pressure medication, but their current BP is down to 85/50 mmHg. What should you do first?

options.A: Hold the medication and notify the physician
options.B: Give the drug with a large glass of water
options.C: Proceed with the dose as ordered on the chart
options.D: Administer half the dose to be safe

explanation: Their blood pressure is already on the lower side! Giving a BP-lowering drug now could cause dangerous crashing, so hold the dose and tell the doctor.

question: How should a good QA committee handle mistakes in the hospital?

options.A: Hide medical errors from the public and media
options.B: Punish staff members immediately when something goes wrong
options.C: Find the root cause and prevent the mistake from happening again
options.D: Focus only on financial losses after an incident

explanation: Brilliant! Modern healthcare focuses on fixing the system so mistakes don't repeat, rather than just blaming people.

question: What is the main activity during the 'Plan' phase of the PDSA cycle?

options.A: Punishing staff who fail to follow new guidelines
options.B: Setting a clear objective and planning how to test a change
options.C: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the ward
options.D: Permanently rewriting all hospital policy rulebooks

explanation: Well done! In the Plan phase, we figure out our goal and decide exactly how we want to run our little test.

question: What is a common oversight that compromises infection control during busy clinic hours?

options.A: Changing examination gloves between every single patient
options.B: Rushing instrument sterilization and processing protocols
options.C: Using too much soap during routine handwashing procedures
options.D: Storing sterile medical supplies in clean cabinets

explanation: You got it! When the clinic gets busy, rushing the autoclaving or cleaning of instruments can leave germs behind and spread infections.

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.A: It automatically increases clinic funding
options.B: It reduces the nurse's ability to show empathy
options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

explanation: When you're exhausted and burnt out, it's so much harder to find the emotional energy to deeply connect with your patients. Take care of yourselves, future nurses!

question: When a low-income Nigerian family faces a sudden medical bill, what is their most common financial backup plan?

options.A: Government health insurance
options.B: Commercial bank loans
options.C: Employer welfare funds
options.D: Extended family networks

explanation: Spot on! Because formal health insurance isn't widespread yet, families usually pull resources together to support sick relatives. You've got this!

question: What is the statistical word for the value that shows up most often in a set of data?

options.A: Range
options.B: Mean
options.C: Median
options.D: Mode

explanation: You got it! Just remember: **Mo**de is the value that appears **mo**st often. Easy peasy!

question: What is the largest organ in the human body?

options.A: The liver
options.B: The skin
options.C: The large intestine
options.D: The skeletal system

explanation: The skin covers the entire external surface of the body, making it the largest single organ by surface area and weight. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which group is often most vulnerable during a disaster due to reliance on continuous care or medical equipment?

options.A: Office workers
options.B: The elderly
options.C: Store owners
options.D: Young adults

explanation: Correct! Older adults often have chronic health needs and rely heavily on steady electricity and support that can fail during a crisis.

question: When a mum gets admitted to the labour ward, why is checking her antenatal card so important?

options.A: To determine the exact time the baby will be born
options.B: To find out if the mother attended antenatal classes regularly
options.C: To identify pre-existing risk factors and review past test results
options.D: To calculate the hospital bill for the delivery service

explanation: Her antenatal card holds secrets to a safe delivery! It shows her blood group, scan results, and any risks we need to watch out for.

question: What is a major risk if a recovering patient stays on a clear liquid diet for too long?

options.A: It triggers sudden weight gain from excess fats
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.C: It permanently ruins the patient's sense of taste
options.D: It can lead to hospital-derived malnutrition due to very low calorie and nutrient content

explanation: Clear liquids are great at first, but they don't have enough energy and nutrients. Keeping patients on them too long starves their healing body!

question: Which of these is a common challenge that ruins a good nursing handover?

options.A: Using the SBAR framework correctly
options.B: Noise, distractions, and staff fatigue
options.C: Having too many standardized reporting templates
options.D: Patients being fully awake and cooperative

question: Which cells are the main ones responsible for humoral immunity?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Cytotoxic T cells
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: B cells

explanation: B cells are the masters of humoral immunity! They mature into plasma cells that pump out circulating antibodies into your body fluids.

question: Which dimension of healthcare quality focuses on preventing injuries from care that is supposed to help?

options.A: Safe care
options.B: Efficient care
options.C: Equitable care
options.D: Timely care

explanation: Spot on! Keeping patients safe means protecting them from accidental harm or injuries while they are receiving treatment in our care.

question: When a nurse scans a patient's medication barcode, which step of the computer cycle is happening?

options.A: Processing
options.B: Storage
options.C: Output
options.D: Input

explanation: Whenever you type, click, or scan something into the computer, you are giving it 'input'. Great job!

question: A researcher decides to pick every 5th patient from the clinic register. Which sampling method is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Convenience sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: You nailed it! Going down a list at regular intervals (like every 5th or 10th person) is called systematic sampling.

question: Why do most patients prefer taking pills by mouth rather than getting injections?

options.A: They always work much faster than injections
options.B: They are completely painless to take
options.C: They are more convenient and avoid needle pain
options.D: They never cause any stomach upset or nausea

explanation: Swallowing pills is much friendlier than skin punctures! It saves patients from needle pain and lets them easily manage their medication routine at home.

question: What do we call the exact spot on an antigen that an antibody latches onto?

options.A: Leukocyte
options.B: Cytokine
options.C: Pathogen
options.D: Epitope

explanation: An epitope is just the specific little target site on an antigen that matches the locking tip of an antibody.

question: Why do nurses need to pay attention to the specific 'strain' of a germ listed in a lab report?

options.A: Different strains within the same species can cause vastly different disease severity
options.B: The strain name tells the nurse which commercial disinfectant to spray
options.C: Only specific strains require nurses to document vital signs hourly
options.D: Strains dictate the exact room temperature required for patient isolation

explanation: Even within the same family of germs, one strain might be harmless while another causes severe illness. Knowing the strain helps you anticipate how sick your patient might get.

question: Which position should an unconscious, non-trauma patient be placed in during transit to prevent aspiration?

options.A: High Fowler's position
options.B: Flat supine position
options.C: Trendelenburg position
options.D: Lateral recovery position

explanation: Turning the patient on their side allows fluids to drain safely out of the mouth instead of blocking the airway. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h4)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient right after placing a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Drink a full glass of water immediately to wash it down.
options.B: Lie flat on your back for at least one hour.
options.C: Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the pill is fully dissolved.
options.D: Chew the tablet quickly to help it enter the bloodstream.

explanation: Eating or drinking washes the medication away before it can absorb through the oral mucosa. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)

question: How does educating a patient help reduce inappropriate drug use?

options.A: It prevents them from ever visiting a hospital clinic again
options.B: It helps them understand why they do not need certain medicines
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to lower medication prices
options.D: It gives them the legal right to prescribe drugs to neighbors

explanation: When patients understand the risks of unnecessary drugs, they are less likely to demand them from clinicians. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do oral contraceptives help clients who suffer from terrible menstrual cramps?

options.A: They relax the urinary bladder muscles
options.B: They thin the uterine lining, reducing prostaglandin release
options.C: They stop all hormone production in the body
options.D: They increase the total volume of menstrual flow

explanation: When the uterine lining stays thinner, it makes fewer prostaglandins—the pesky chemicals that cause those painful uterine cramps during your period.

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for nurses working on a hospital ward?

options.A: All medical equipment is padded to prevent physical injuries
options.B: Staff can report errors and voice concerns without fear of punishment
options.C: Nurses never experience emotional stress during their shifts
options.D: Patients are locked inside their rooms to prevent accidental falls

explanation: Psychological safety means you feel safe speaking up about a mistake or sharing a worry without being yelled at. It helps everyone learn!

question: A patient takes a standard dose of an antibiotic they've used safely before, but suddenly develops a severe skin rash. What type of reaction is this?

options.A: Type A Augmented reaction
options.B: A normal therapeutic response
options.C: Type B Bizarre reaction
options.D: A simple medication overdose

question: Why do injuries to tendons and ligaments take such a long time to heal?

options.A: They lack any nervous tissue to signal the brain about pain
options.B: They are constantly exposed to strong digestive enzymes
options.C: They have a relatively poor blood supply compared to other tissues
options.D: They are made entirely of dead cells that cannot replicate

explanation: Blood brings the healing nutrients! Because tendons and ligaments get less blood flow, repairs happen much more slowly.

question: What is the primary function of plasmin during the healing process?

options.A: It breaks down and dissolves the fibrin clot
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of new platelets
options.C: It causes the initial vascular spasm in injured vessels
options.D: It converts inactive prothrombin into active thrombin

explanation: Plasmin is the active enzyme responsible for digesting fibrin strands so the body can clear away old, unneeded clots. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why did ancient people use fermentation for baking and brewing long before anyone discovered microbes?

options.A: They followed strict written instructions left by early microbiologists
options.B: They observed the practical results of microbial action without knowing the cause
options.C: They accidentally stumbled upon chemicals that preserved food permanently
options.D: They possessed advanced microscopes made of polished river stones

explanation: Ancient folks didn't know about germs yet, but they knew bread dough rises and palm wine ferments through trial and observation! Great job.

question: A community refuses to bring sick relatives to the clinic because of rumors that nurses cause infections. How should you respond?

options.A: Ignore the community and wait until they come voluntarily
options.B: Threaten the villagers with police arrest for disobedience
options.C: Engage community leaders with clear, respectful health education
options.D: Close down the primary health center until they apologize

explanation: Wonderful nursing approach! Building trust through community leaders and patient education is key to clearing up dangerous rumors.

question: What is the main chemical difference between vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Vitamins contain heavy metal ions instead of carbon
options.B: Minerals are fragile organic compounds destroyed by cooking
options.C: Minerals are inorganic elements that lack carbon-hydrogen bonds
options.D: Vitamins are solid metallic rocks found naturally in soil

explanation: Correct! Minerals are pure elemental substances from the earth, while vitamins are complex organic molecules made by living things.

question: What is the main goal of pasteurizing commercial milk?

options.A: To increase the natural sugar and fat percentages
options.B: To destroy all disease-causing pathogens safely
options.C: To remove every single living microbe and spore
options.D: To convert all liquid milk completely into cheese

explanation: You got it! Pasteurization uses heat to knock out harmful germs so the milk is safe to drink, even though it doesn't kill every single spore.

question: What is a crucial safety check before using any mechanical lift sling?

options.A: Ensuring the patient is wearing non-skid slippers
options.B: Inspecting the straps and clips for fraying or damage
options.C: Measuring the exact distance to the hallway door
options.D: Checking if the battery is fully charged to maximum speed

explanation: Always double-check those straps! Frayed or worn fabric can snap under pressure, which is dangerous for the patient in the sling.

question: A patient wants a daily pill to prevent getting HIV before any potential exposure. What is this prevention method called?

options.A: Syndromic management protocol
options.B: Contact tracing therapy
options.C: Pre-exposure prophylaxis
options.D: Post-exposure prophylaxis

question: What is a key instruction the nurse must give the patient before the procedure starts?

options.A: Take deep breaths continuously while the needle is in place
options.B: Remain as still as possible and avoid coughing during insertion
options.C: Stand up and walk around the room to help settle the fluid
options.D: Drink at least two liters of water right before the procedure

question: Which tissue type burns more calories at rest?

options.A: Bone matrix
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Muscle tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

options.A: It forbids patients from seeing private medical doctors
options.B: It is completely managed by the Ministry of Health
options.C: It is strictly limited to retired civil servants
options.D: It is provided by companies as part of worker compensation

explanation: Spot on! Employer-sponsored plans are job benefits where companies help cover or fully pay health insurance for their staff.

question: Why are nurses in a great position to spot patients who need DRF exemptions?

options.A: They make the final legal decisions on hospital budgets
options.B: They personally purchase all the drugs sold in the pharmacy
options.C: They are responsible for auditing the hospital's bank accounts
options.D: They spend the most direct time at the patient's bedside

explanation: Because nurses are constantly at the bedside, they are the first to notice when a patient is struggling to afford their prescribed medications.

question: What is the primary focus of organisational objectives in healthcare?

options.A: The private business ventures of senior medical doctors
options.B: The daily social events organised by the nursing union
options.C: The personal retirement plans of individual staff members
options.D: The survival, growth, and overall service delivery of the institution

explanation: Organzational objectives look at the big picture—keeping the hospital running smoothly, growing, and providing great care to the community.

question: What is an early sign of developing shock that you should watch out for in trauma patients?

options.A: High urine output
options.B: Altered mental status and cool skin
options.C: Warm, flushed skin
options.D: Slow and deep breathing

explanation: You nailed it. When the body goes into shock, blood gets pulled away from the skin and brain, making the patient feel anxious or confused with cool, clammy hands.

question: As a nurse, what simple and effective practice should you teach community members in areas with unsafe water?

options.A: Avoiding all handwashing to save clean water
options.B: Using untreated river water for infant formula
options.C: Boiling drinking water before consumption
options.D: Adding industrial solvents to kill local algae

explanation: Correct! Boiling is a cheap, reliable way families can kill germs at home when tap or well water isn't safe.

question: Why is having a solid backup plan to a hospital so important for home birth programs?

options.A: Most women prefer to give birth in a hospital eventually
options.B: Emergency situations can develop unexpectedly during labor
options.C: Community health nurses are not allowed to deliver babies alone
options.D: Hospitals require proof of home birth for birth certificates

explanation: Childbirth can take sudden turns! That's why having a fast, reliable link to a hospital is a must-have safety net just in case complications pop up.

question: Why does the body need to metabolize drugs, especially fat-soluble ones?

options.A: To make fat-soluble drugs easier for the kidneys to excrete
options.B: To completely prevent medications from entering the bloodstream
options.C: To make all drugs stay inside fatty tissues forever
options.D: To turn every drug into a permanent fat-soluble storage form

question: How should you clean a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Wiping in a circular motion from the center outward and letting it dry
options.B: Applying an antiseptic spray and immediately inserting the needle
options.C: Wiping from the outer edges inward toward the center of the site
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth with a dry cotton ball

explanation: Always move from clean (center) to less clean (outward) to push germs away. Plus, letting the alcohol dry is what actually kills the microbes!

question: Which statement best describes the role of nurse managers when using scheduling software?

options.A: They have no control over the roster once the computer generates it
options.B: They are only responsible for entering patient billing data into the system
options.C: They stop working night shifts completely because software handles them
options.D: They must still review and adjust schedules for human factors and emergencies

explanation: Software assists with the math, but nurse managers must use clinical judgment for unexpected personal situations. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: What does a level one priority indicate on a standard emergency triage scale?

options.A: An infection requiring oral antibiotics only
options.B: Immediate life-threatening resuscitation needed
options.C: A stable patient ready for immediate discharge
options.D: A minor non-urgent medical complaint

question: What are the three classic steps in Kurt Lewin's model of change?

options.A: Unfreezing, moving, and refreezing

options.C: Planning, executing, and evaluating
options.D: Assessing, diagnosing, and treating

question: Why is the community nurse so vital in settings with limited resources?

options.A: They replace the need for any secondary or tertiary healthcare facilities

options.C: They serve as the first line of defense to stabilize rapidly deteriorating patients before hospital transfer
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers legally permitted to perform major surgeries

explanation: Spotting danger signs early and starting care right away makes all the difference when a patient arrives at a local clinic first.

question: Which of the following is a major systemic challenge facing health promotion programs in Nigeria?

options.B: Too many well-funded hospitals with no patients to treat
options.C: Brain drain of skilled healthcare professionals leaving the country
options.D: Zero interest from local communities in improving their health
